models.notes: Bandai publishes no odds and no slot list. English pack = 12 cards, box = 24 packs, case = 12 boxes (confirmed). The C/UC/leader/rare split of the 12 cards (7 C + 3 UC + 1 leader-or-common + 1 rare-or-better) is a structural ESTIMATE; it only moves bulk value. SR/SEC/alt-art/SP/Manga rates are community figures (OP-04 12-box case tally; OP15/16/17 case-opening pages) and vary by set. TCGplayer labels: rarity is the BASE rarity even for alternates (C, UC, R, SR, SEC, L, TR, PR, DON!!); variants are told apart only by name suffix: '(Alternate Art)' and '(Parallel)' = parallels, '(SP)', '(Manga)', '(Wanted Poster)', '(Super Alternate Art)', '(Red Super Alternate Art)', '(Gold)', '(Silver)', '(Pirate Foil)', '(Reprint)'. name_regex values are Python/JS-compatible; NOSUF is a negative-lookahead meaning 'plain card without those suffixes'. A card named e.g. 'Luffy (001)' (leader number) counts as plain. TCGplayer finishes in English prints: C, UC and base L are Normal; R, SR, SEC, TR, DON!! and all alt-art variants are Foil. OP-13 specials (Super/Red Super Alternate Art, Wanted Poster, 'Character Edition' SPs) have no measured rate; they are lumped into the SEC-alt and SP outcomes, so OP-13 EV is probably understated. The Japanese-box pages (6-card packs) were not used for rates except as a cross-check. EB sets have fewer commons (e.g. 21 C in EB05) so their real slot layout probably differs; treat EB as 'estimate'.

applies_to.description: English TCG core boosters with 1-of-each Quarter Century Secret Rare alternates (100-101 cards: 50 C, 26 SR, 14 UR, 10 Secret + QCSR). Excludes Quarter Century Bonanza/Stampede, Rarity Collection, Maze of Millennia.

outcomes.note: Dotesports: 'one or two' per box (0.04-0.08 per pack); 1.5/24 used. Each is an alternate version of an Ultra/Secret card, taken 2:1 from the Ultra and Secret outcomes.

models.notes: Structure since Eternity Code (April 2020): 8 Commons + 1 'higher-rarity' card; that card is 3/4 Super Rare, 1/6 Ultra Rare, 1/12 Secret Rare (Yugipedia Core Booster page; an English 8-box sample of Maze of Muertos independently shows UR ~1 in 6 and Secret ~1 in 12). The older '7 commons + 1 Rare + 1 foil' layout ended in 2020, and these sets have NO 'Rare' rarity at all. Konami publishes no odds; the table is community/wiki-documented, hence not 'official'. QCSR rate is the weak point: 1 per box is the common claim, Dotesports says 1-2 per box. EV of QCSR chase cards ($20-100+) is sensitive to it. TCGplayer rarity labels: Common, Super Rare, Ultra Rare, Secret Rare, Quarter Century Secret Rare (separate product named '<card> (Quarter Century Secret Rare)'). TCGplayer finishes: '1st Edition' (main), 'Unlimited' and 'Limited' exist for a few cards - use 1st Edition. Odds within a rarity assumed equal across cards of that rarity (some prints also have 'Platinum'/'Ultimate' style extras only in special sets, not core).

models.notes: Same 8 Commons + 1 final card structure; Starlight is an alternate version of an Ultra or Secret card, not a separate slot (TCGTalk). Blazing Dominion sample (English, ~240 packs, TCGTalk): Super Rare ~1 in 3 packs (7-8/box), Ultra ~1 in 6, Secret ~1 in 12, Starlight ~1 in 72. Ultra/Secret/Starlight agree with the wiki table; the SR figure does NOT (3/4 of 24 packs = 18 SR per box vs 7-8 reported). The wiki structure (8 Commons + 1 card that is at least Super Rare) is kept because it is what the TCGplayer article also states ('guaranteed to contain at least a Super Rare, in addition to eight Commons'); the TCGTalk SR number is probably a loose estimate. If you want to hedge, EV difference is only (0.75-0.33) x avg Super Rare price per pack. Starlight rate is from one set (1/3 per box); the older Legendary Arc-V Decks page shows 1 per 5-6 boxes for a different product. Labels/finish as in the QCSR-era model; Starlight is 'Starlight Rare' on TCGplayer.

models.notes: Riot does not print odds. Layout (retail listing + riftbound.gg): 7 Common, 3 Uncommon, 2 Rare-or-better, 1 foil of any rarity, 1 token/Rune = 14. TCGplayer shows Rare, Epic and Showcase as Foil-only products (Vendetta data) and Common/Uncommon with both Normal and Foil rows, which matches 'two foil rare-or-better slots + one foil slot'. Epic ~1 in 4 packs replaces a Rare (Origins estimate 25%; Vendetta/Radiance 168-186 pack samples 27%). Showcase Alternate Art 1 per 12 packs (Origins) vs ~9-10% (samples). Overnumbered 1 per 72 packs (Riot-attributed) vs 1.6% sample. Signed Overnumbered ~1 in 10 Overnumbered. The two TCGTalk pages report near-identical numbers and may share data - treat as ONE sample. Ultimate rarity (Radiance 'Packed Amphitheater', Riot-stated 0.025%) and the Unleashed 'Baron Nashor' chase are not modeled. Foil-slot rarity mix is an assumption. TCGplayer rarity labels: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Showcase; Showcase variants are named '(Alternate Art)', '(Overnumbered)', '(Signature)', and Runes 'Fury Rune (R01a)'. A rare Epic with '(Alternate Art)' (1 per set) is labeled Epic, negligible.

notes: Built 2026-10-20 from public web pages and tcgcsv.com TCGplayer data. Rarity names are the exact TCGplayer labels; for One Piece, Star Wars Unlimited, Riftbound, Digimon and DBS the TCGplayer rarity is the BASE rarity and variants (alt art, hyperspace, showcase...) are separate products identified by a name suffix, so name_regex is essential. name_regex values are Python/JS-compatible regexes matched against the TCGplayer product name; when absent, match by rarity only. Extra keys beyond the format spec (safe to ignore): per-outcome 'basis' / 'note', per-model 'packs_per_box', top-level 'unmodeled'. Outcomes with rarity [] carry no value (tokens, basic Runes, filler). In every model within-rarity odds are assumed equal across the cards that match the outcome. No game here has OFFICIAL odds; only SWU (launch set) and the Yu-Gi-Oh/Lorcana/FaB pack layouts come from the publisher or its wiki. Every rate is a community figure unless stated. Weakest points: Lorcana Iconic and Enchanted rates; One Piece Manga/SP/alt-art; Yu-Gi-Oh QCSR and Starlight; SWU Hyperspace Foil rarity mix; FaB Majestic/Marvel; Digimon, UA, DBS, Gundam slot layouts; Weiss has no model.
